verdict: Looks polished and professional. Desktop is a balanced 3-zone layout (dice stage left, VRF panel right, route + history below); the eyebrow/heading rhythm is clean and the green accent is used with restraint. Mobile stacks cleanly with the dice stage on top. The one soft spot is the left dice stage: a small 168px white cube floats in a much larger 330px dashed-framed teal panel, so there is a lot of dead space inside that frame on first paint.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholder shows for empty Stake ('--'), 'No local roll history yet.' empty state is present, the status bar with localized status + payout reads cleanly, and preset/withdraw affordances survived. No regressions seen.

findings.title: Dice stage frame is mostly empty on first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the left teal panel (dashed inner border) is ~330px tall but only holds a small ~168px cube showing '6' and a bottom caption pill, leaving a large empty band above/around the cube. PlayArea.scss:61-98 sets .dice-stage__visual min-height:330px with a min(168px,42vw) cube, so the cube occupies under half the frame height.
findings.fix: Either grow the cube (e.g. width min(220px, 56%)) so it better fills the frame, or reduce .dice-stage__visual min-height to ~260px and tighten the dashed inset so the empty band shrinks. Optionally add the chosen-face label or 1/6 odds chip inside the frame to fill it with relevant content.

findings.title: Current-stake caption duplicates the right-panel Stake tile
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the bottom-left caption pill reads 'CURRENT STAKE 0.1 GAS' while the top-right summary already shows a 'Stake 0.1 GAS' tile — the same value is rendered twice within one viewport. PlayArea.tsx:146-149 (caption) and :240-243 (summary Stake tile).
findings.fix: Repurpose the in-stage caption to show something non-redundant (e.g. selected face + potential payout, or the live 'Ready/Rolling' state) so the two zones complement rather than repeat each other.

verdict: Clean, confident coin-flip UI: layered glassy coin with orbit rings, clear Heads/Tails cards, preset chips, and a strong full-width green Flip CTA. Empty 'No games played yet' state with a clock icon is friendly. Desktop renders as a single ~520px centered column, leaving wide empty white margins on both sides on a desktop viewport — acceptable for a focused game but it reads small. The main clarity gap is the coin/side symbology.
round1_held: Yes. Stats row (0 wins/losses/games, 0.00 GAS), house-cap hint ('House can currently pay up to 100.00 GAS'), custom bet input, and empty history all render correctly. The live choice binding fix (str('choice')) is intact. No regressions.

findings.title: Coin face uses 'N'/'G' glyphs for Heads/Tails without a legend
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile screenshots: the hero coin shows a large 'N' and the choice cards show 'N' (labeled Heads) and 'G' (labeled Tails). Nothing on screen tells the player that N=Neo=Heads and G=Gas=Tails; WagerControls.tsx:44 maps heads->'N', tails->'G'. A first-time player sees a coin reading 'N' and an unlabeled hero and must infer the metaphor.
findings.fix: Either render the actual 'Heads'/'Tails' word (or a coin-face icon) on the hero coin instead of a bare 'N', or add a small caption under the coin ('N = Heads / G = Tails') so the brand glyph is decoded. Keeping the N/G on the choice cards is fine since they are labeled, but the standalone hero coin glyph is ambiguous.

findings.title: Hero coin lacks a visible side/state label on first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the coin sits above a small 'Place Your Bet' pill, but the coin itself shows only 'N' with no caption tying it to the selected side — on a large desktop the big white arena card around the coin feels under-filled (CoinArena.tsx renders coin + a single status pill).
findings.fix: Surface the selected side text near the coin (e.g. 'You picked: Heads') and/or add the 2x payout preview chip inside the arena so the hero communicates the current bet, filling the card and reinforcing the choice.

verdict: The hero (gradient band, 'Live market status' dot, MACHINES/YOUR PULLS/EST. PLAYS metrics with an em-dash for unknown) is clean and on-brand. The empty market state is clear with a good two-button recovery (Refresh Machines / Open Studio). The weak points are the letter-glyph 'G' avatars that read like missing images, and a very tall expanse of blank page below the empty-state card on desktop.
round1_held: Yes. MACHINES shows an em-dash placeholder (not 0/N/A), metrics are friendly, 'NO ACTIVE MACHINES LOADED' empty state with dual CTAs is present, and the Create Machine action is visible. No regressions.

findings.title: Letter-glyph 'G' avatars read as broken/placeholder images
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile screenshots: the hero badge and the empty-state circle both show a plain bold letter 'G' in a tinted circle. PlayArea.tsx:314 (hero 'G'), :357 (empty-state 'G'), and machineIcon() at :292-297 returns single letters 'G'/'P'/'N'. A solo letter in a circle looks like a fallback for a missing logo rather than an intentional icon.
findings.fix: Replace the single-letter glyphs with a real SVG mark (a gachapon/blind-box icon) for the hero and empty state, matching the inline SVG icon style used by sibling apps (e.g. fogplay's coin SVG, last-survivor's timer glyph). Keep letters only where they encode rarity tiers if desired, but the hero/empty avatars should be iconographic.

findings.title: Empty market state leaves a tall blank page below on desktop
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the hero + 'No active machines loaded' card end around y=560, then the rest of the viewport down to ~900px is pure white with no content or footer. The empty state card is short and centered, so the page looks unfinished on a wide screen.
findings.fix: Vertically center the empty-state content within the available space, or add a lightweight 'how GasBox works' / sample-machine teaser strip beneath the empty card so the first paint fills the viewport instead of trailing into blank space.

verdict: The creator workspace is a tidy two-column form (Create reward pool | Pool controls) with clear uppercase field labels and an em-dash-free, calm look. But the right column has a visual-hierarchy problem: five identical full-width solid-green pill buttons (Inspect pool, Add GAS, Recover remaining GAS, Check credit, Withdraw credit) all shout at equal volume, and there is a large empty gap between the hint box and the first button, leaving the right column unbalanced and button-heavy versus the left form column.
round1_held: Yes. The 'Enter a pool ID to inspect, top up, or recover...' hint, the 'RECOVERABLE GAS 0 GAS' credit block, and the collapsed 'Campaign owner setup' details survived. Buttons correctly disabled-styled (lighter green) when no pool target. No regressions.

findings.title: Five identical full-width green buttons give no action hierarchy
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: Inspect pool / Add GAS / Recover remaining GAS / Check credit / Withdraw credit are all rendered as the same solid-green rounded pill at full width. PlayArea.tsx:569-615 — every one uses className='gas-pool-claim-only__button', and .gas-pool-claim-only__button (PlayArea.scss:263-291) is a single solid #16c784 style with no secondary/ghost variant. Nothing signals which is the primary action; the column reads as a wall of green.
findings.fix: Differentiate by role: keep 'Inspect pool' as the solid-green primary, demote 'Add GAS' / 'Recover remaining GAS' / 'Check credit' / 'Withdraw credit' to outline or soft-fill secondary variants (green text on tinted bg). This also visually separates the destructive 'Recover' from the benign 'Inspect'.

findings.title: Unbalanced columns: empty gap in right column, short left column
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: in the right 'Pool controls' card there is a tall empty band between the hint box (~y=237) and the first button (~y=290), while the action buttons cluster in the lower half; meanwhile the left 'Create reward pool' card ends well above the right card's bottom. The two cards have visibly different fill density. .gas-pool-actions uses grid 1fr/1fr (PlayArea.scss:563-567) but the buttons render stacked, amplifying the vertical imbalance.
findings.fix: Tighten the right column: place Inspect/Add GAS/Recover in a 2-up grid row directly under the inputs (remove the large gap), and group Check/Withdraw credit inside the RECOVERABLE GAS card as a compact pair. Align both card heights or let the form column breathe so the columns read as a balanced pair.

verdict: Strong game hero: circular countdown ring, TOTAL POT tile, SAFE->CRITICAL danger meter, a clean keys stepper with preset chips, and a tidy YOUR KEYS / TOTAL KEYS / SHARE strip with a '—' share placeholder. The empty 'No events yet' history is fine. The standout problem is redundancy: the first paint stacks three separate 'Refresh Round' prompts, which clutters the otherwise clean flow.
round1_held: Yes. The 'Round state unavailable' service notice with localized copy, the SHARE '—' em-dash placeholder, the calm (non-pulsing) fresh-round danger ring, and the disabled Buy Keys with helper text all held. No regressions.

findings.title: Three stacked 'Refresh Round' affordances on first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot shows, top to bottom: (1) the amber 'Round state unavailable' card with a 'Refresh Round' button, (3) a 'Rollover ready / Refresh the game state before buying keys' card with another 'Refresh Round' button, and (2) the Buy Keys card with 'Refresh the round state before submitting a key purchase' helper + disabled Buy Keys. PlayArea.tsx:125-143 (serviceNotice card), :210-232 (round-control-card, renders when !isRoundActive), and the BuyKeysCard helper buyKeysHelper at :90-94 all surface a refresh prompt simultaneously.
findings.fix: Collapse to one refresh entry point. When serviceNotice is present, suppress the separate round-control-card (they both say 'refresh'), and let the Buy Keys helper reference that single notice rather than repeating the instruction. Show at most one 'Refresh Round' button above the fold.

findings.title: Disabled Buy Keys button is low-contrast and reads as inert filler
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the 'Buy Keys' button (below 'Refresh the round state before submitting a key purchase') is a pale grey full-width bar with light grey text, nearly blending into the card background. PlayArea.tsx:194-208 renders BuyKeysCard with disabled={!canBuyKeys}; in the disconnected state it is permanently disabled and visually flat.
findings.fix: Give the disabled primary a clearer disabled treatment (e.g. retain a faint green tint + visible label, or swap the disabled CTA for the 'Refresh Round' secondary action so the only enabled control is obvious). Ensure the disabled label keeps AA contrast against the bar.

verdict: Desktop reads clean and on-brand: soft green hero, a 3-card spread with branded NEO card backs, and a clear question field. The weak spot is the right column — the 'Transaction safety' panel holds ~3 lines of text but visually stretches tall, leaving a large empty void beside the spread. Mobile reflows well into a single column with the hero, question, and spread stacked.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders ('—') render in the outer empty card captions, the withdraw-credit recovery panel is wired (prepaidCredit gate), and the friendlier 'Submit a question first' / 'Request ready' labels are present. No regressions.

findings.title: Right column collapses to a near-empty tall panel on desktop (unbalanced columns)
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the right 'TRANSACTION SAFETY' card holds only 3 short lines yet the right grid track is as tall as the left workspace, leaving a big empty area under the text. On first paint the recovery panel is gated off (prepaidCredit==0) so the aside has just one short card. PlayArea.scss:24-32 sets `.tarot-shell` to a fixed 2-col grid (0.72fr / 0.44fr) with `align-items: start`, so the side column has nothing to fill its width.
findings.fix: On first paint give the side column more substance or let it shrink: either move the READINGS/CARDS-DRAWN metric tiles into the aside so the right column has real content, or reduce the side track width (e.g. minmax(280px, 0.36fr)) and let the main workspace breathe. Alternatively collapse to a single column below ~1200px instead of 900px so the void never appears at common desktop widths.

findings.title: Empty-spread captions mix em-dash and instructional text inconsistently
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the PAST and FUTURE card slots show a bare '—' caption while the center PRESENT slot shows 'Submit a question first'. PlayArea.tsx:153-157 renders the hint only for index===1 and '—' for the others. The three identical card backs with two different caption styles reads slightly uneven.
findings.fix: Either show the 'Submit a question first' hint once centered beneath the whole spread (not under the middle card), or give all three slots the same muted caption treatment so the row reads as one consistent empty state.

verdict: Desktop is strong and well-structured: hero stat strip, a clear dormant-season banner, an amber 'data unavailable' notice, a burn form with presets and a 4-up impact strip, and a centered empty leaderboard. Mobile is mostly good but the 4-column impact strip breaks down — it wraps into a cramped 2x2 where vertical dividers float between items and two-line labels ('PROJECTED TOTAL', 'PRIZE POOL') collide with the values of the row above.
round1_held: Yes. The localized 'Burn league data unavailable' service notice, the season lifecycle banner with settle path, the soft-tinted disabled CTA, and the boxed empty leaderboard state all render correctly. No regressions.

findings.title: Impact strip wraps into a cramped, divider-littered grid on mobile
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshot bottom: the ENTRY AMOUNT / PROJECTED TOTAL / PROJECTED RANK / PRIZE POOL strip wraps to 2x2; the vertical 1px dividers (`.burn-league-impact-divider`, width:1px; margin:2px 16px) stay in the flex flow between wrapped items, and the two-word labels wrap to a second line so 'PROJECTED TOTAL' sits on top of the row below's value. PlayArea.scss:396-437 uses `flex-wrap: wrap` with `flex: 1 1 80px` items plus inline dividers, and there is no mobile rule to convert it to a clean grid.
findings.fix: Add a mobile breakpoint (≤480px or ≤560px) that switches `.burn-league-impact-strip` to `display:grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap:12px` and sets `.burn-league-impact-divider { display:none }`. Give each item a min-height so the wrapped two-line labels don't overlap neighboring values.

findings.title: Hero rank fact never appears, leaving the hero right side stat-only
findings.evidence: PlayArea.tsx:150-158 only renders the inline 'YOUR RANK' fact when hasRank is true (formattedRank !== '--'). In the disconnected first paint (desktop + mobile screenshots) it is absent, which is correct, but the hero subtitle 'Burn tokens, earn rewards' is the only copy beneath the title — the hero reads thin next to the three stat tiles. Acceptable as an empty state, just flagging the imbalance.
findings.fix: Optional: when there is no rank yet, show a one-line value-prop or 'Be the first to burn this season' microcopy in the hero-copy block so the left side is not just title+subtitle against three populated stat tiles.

verdict: A tidy claim-first surface: branded envelope hero, three metric tiles, a Claim/Create tab, and a muted 'No active envelopes' panel. The redundant 'ACTIVE ENVELOPES' label (top metric tile and the activity panel heading both say it with '0') and the very pale disabled 'Claim now' button are the two things that pull it down. Mobile stacks the three metric tiles into three full-width rows which eats a lot of vertical space for three zeros.
round1_held: Yes. The em-dash/'—' is not used here but the friendly empty-state line, the soft-tinted disabled CTA, the share-link affordance, and the reclaim/withdraw recovery panel (gated) are all in place. No regressions.

findings.title: 'Active envelopes' label appears twice with the same '0' value
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the first metric tile reads 'ACTIVE ENVELOPES 0' and lower the activity panel heading also reads 'ACTIVE ENVELOPES 0'. messages.ts shows `availableEnvelopes` and `availablePools` both resolve to 'Active envelopes' (en), and PlayArea.tsx:201 + :371 render both. Two identical labels/values on one screen reads as a duplication bug.
findings.fix: Rename the lower activity-panel heading so it describes the list, e.g. 'Available to claim' or 'Open envelopes' (change the `availablePools` string, not `availableEnvelopes`), so the metric tile and the list section no longer collide on the same words.

findings.title: Disabled 'Claim now' CTA is very low-contrast pale green on first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile screenshots: with no envelope ID entered the 'Claim now' button is a faint pale-green-on-pale-green pill (PlayArea.tsx:270 disables it when selectedEnvelopeId is empty; PlayArea.scss:370-377 styles disabled primary as violet-soft bg + violet-strong text at opacity 0.85). The green-text-on-green-soft fill barely meets contrast and reads almost as placeholder, making it unclear it is a button.
findings.fix: Bump the disabled-state contrast: use a muted ink text (e.g. --ns-text-muted) on the soft fill instead of accent-green-on-accent-soft, or raise opacity and darken the label so the control is legibly a (currently inactive) button.

findings.title: Three metric tiles stack into three full-width rows on mobile
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshot: ACTIVE ENVELOPES, CLAIMABLE POOL, RECENT CLAIMS each become a full-width card stacked vertically, consuming ~3 rows of height for three zeros before the user reaches the Claim form. PlayArea.scss:690-695 collapses `.redenv-metrics` to `grid-template-columns: 1fr` at ≤640px.
findings.fix: Keep the metrics as a denser layout on mobile — e.g. a single horizontal 3-up row of compact tiles (grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) with smaller padding/font) so the primary Claim action stays above the fold.

verdict: Clean and balanced first paint: a green-tinted hero with the social badge and a single full-width 'New Contract' form card with stake/duration preset chips, character counters, and a disabled 'Create Contract' button. It looks like a real product form. The main weakness on wide desktop is the hero — badge + two short lines sit far left, leaving ~60% of the hero empty since the metrics line is gated off pre-contract.
round1_held: Yes. Inline validation (partner/stake/duration), character counters, the action-notice slot, the gated credit-recovery card, and the gated contracts list are all present and the form preserves input on failure. No regressions.

findings.title: Hero is left-weighted and mostly empty on wide desktop
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the hero card spans the full 1040px width but only the badge + 'Breakup Contract' + 'Relationship stakes on-chain' sit at the left; the right ~60% is blank because `.breakup-hero-metrics` (PlayArea.tsx:105) is gated behind hasContracts and is absent on first paint. The hero gradient (PlayArea.scss:82) makes the empty right side read as unused space.
findings.fix: On the empty/first-paint state, either narrow the hero content max-width so it doesn't stretch the full card, or add a quiet right-aligned value-prop chip (e.g. 'Stake-backed · On-chain · Refundable') so the hero feels intentional rather than half-filled.

findings.title: Tall empty canvas below the form on desktop
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: below the 'Create Contract' button there is a large blank area to the bottom of the viewport because the contracts list and credit card are both gated off on first paint, and `.breakup-play-area` is `min-height: 100vh` (PlayArea.scss:62). The page reads as a short form floating at the top of a tall empty page.
findings.fix: Drop the `min-height: 100vh` on the root (let content define height), or add a lightweight 'How it works / what happens on break' explainer card beneath the form for the empty state so the lower viewport is not a void.

verdict: Desktop is a polished two-column layout: hero with three stat tiles, a friendly robot empty state under 'Top Developers' with a 'How it works' disclosure, and a Send Tip form + Developer Zone on the right. It looks good, but the two columns are clearly unbalanced — the right column (Send Tip + Developer Zone) is noticeably taller than the left, and the disabled 'Send Tip' button is very pale green on first paint. Mobile correctly reorders the Send Tip form above the developer list.
round1_held: Yes. The withdraw-tips path, the stranded-credit reclaim row (gated by myCredit), the stale-zero total guard (PlayArea.tsx:50-53), the segmented anonymous toggle, and localized empty-state copy are all present. No regressions.

findings.title: Unbalanced two columns leave whitespace beside the empty developer list
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the left column (TOP DEVELOPERS robot empty state + 'How it works' bar) ends well above the right column (Send Tip card + Developer Zone). `.tipping-body` (PlayArea.scss:193-198) is a 1.4fr/1fr grid with `align-items: start`, so on first paint the shorter side leaves an awkward column of empty space, and the overall page bottom is ragged.
findings.fix: Balance the first-paint heights: e.g. let the empty-state card grow (min-height to roughly match the right column), or move 'How it works' to span full width beneath both columns, or reduce the left/right ratio so the empty developer panel and the form read as a more even pair.

findings.title: Disabled 'Send Tip' CTA is faint pale-green and reads as non-interactive on first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile screenshots: with no developer selected and no amount, 'Send Tip' renders as pale-green text on pale-green fill (TipForm canSubmit false → disabled; PlayArea.scss:704-710 styles disabled primary as tip-accent-soft bg + tip-accent-strong text at opacity 0.85). The low green-on-green contrast plus no inline 'enter a developer ID first' hint makes it ambiguous why the button is inactive.
findings.fix: Raise the disabled-state contrast (muted ink label on the soft fill, or darker text), and add a one-line helper under the form like 'Enter a registered developer ID and amount to tip' so the disabled CTA's reason is explicit in the empty state.

verdict: Clean, centered, well-composed empty state. The hero card (green check badge, ESCROWS eyebrow, title, subtitle, three boxed stat tiles) reads as intentional, and the 'Contract deployment pending' notice below is a tidy icon+title+description card. Desktop and mobile both reflow correctly with no edge-touching or overflow. Looks professional; main weakness is the three identical dash placeholders in the stat row.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders are present in the stat tiles (no error-like 0), the deployment-pending empty state is friendly and localized, and the column is capped at 760px and centered so the sparse state doesn't read as an under-filled canvas.

findings.title: Three hero stat tiles are visually indistinguishable at first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop+mobile shots: the ESCROWS / ACTIVE / COMPLETED tiles each show the same bold heavy '—' in identical 22px/800 type (MilestoneHero.tsx:34-47, .hero-stat-value at PlayArea.scss:116). Three identical dashes side-by-side read as redundant filler rather than three distinct metrics; the row carries weight but no information.
findings.fix: At the empty state, lighten the placeholder dash (use --me-muted color + lighter weight for the '—' specifically, e.g. a .hero-stat-value--empty modifier) so the tiles read as 'awaiting data' rather than three equal bold values; or collapse to a single subtle 'No escrows yet' line until totalEscrows>0, mirroring how the progress band is already hidden when hasEscrows is false.

findings.title: Notice icon and hero badge share the same green circle treatment
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the hero uses a green check in a soft-green circle, and the 'Contract deployment pending' notice uses an alert (!) glyph in the same soft-green circle (.hero-badge PlayArea.scss:52-61 and .escrow-notice__icon:507-517 share --me-accent-soft bg + --me-accent-strong fg). A blocking/pending notice rendered in the brand's positive green reads as reassuring rather than cautionary.
findings.fix: Give the deployment-pending notice icon a neutral/amber tint (e.g. a warning token) instead of brand green so the 'pending/blocked' meaning isn't colored as success; keep green for the hero success badge only.

verdict: The richest layout in the cluster and it holds together well: two-column desktop shell (custody form + Signers/Execution route/Recent Activity aside), thin gradient hero with three fact tiles, clean step labels. Mobile stacks correctly. The one thing that genuinely looks off is the primary 'Create Vault' button rendering as a barely-visible pale-green-on-pale-green pill, plus first-paint clutter from × buttons on three empty signer rows.
round1_held: Yes. 'Connect a wallet to create or sign' line, em-dash placeholders in VAULT BALANCE / REQUEST hero tiles, the contextual blocked-reason hint ('Add at least two signer addresses before creating a vault'), and the soft-tinted disabled CTA are all present.

findings.title: Disabled 'Create Vault' primary CTA is too low-contrast to read
findings.evidence: Desktop+mobile shots: the main 'Create Vault' button is a pale mint pill with light-green text and a faint hairline border — at first paint it's hard to tell it's the primary action; it nearly disappears into the white form. Source confirms this is the disabled style: .multisig-primary-actions .neo-btn--primary:disabled sets background:--multisig-green-soft, color:--multisig-green-strong, opacity:0.85 (PlayArea.scss:566-572). Green-on-green at 0.85 opacity fails comfortable contrast for button text.
findings.fix: Either remove opacity:0.85 and darken the disabled text to --multisig-green-strong at full opacity on a slightly deeper soft-green, or keep the disabled fill but add a visible 1px solid border in --multisig-green so the button shape is unambiguous. The goal: the disabled primary should still clearly read as 'the button you'll press once the form is valid.'

findings.title: × remove buttons clutter three empty signer rows on first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop+mobile shots: all three default signer inputs are empty (placeholder 'Neo N3 address (N...)') yet each carries a square × remove button on its right (rendered whenever canRemoveSigner, i.e. signers.length>2 — PlayArea.tsx:332-341). Removing an already-empty row is a no-op affordance and the three ×'s add visual noise to an empty form.
findings.fix: Only show the × on rows that have content, or hide it on the minimum required rows until a 4th signer is added (e.g. show remove only when signers.length>MIN_SIGNERS AND the row is non-empty). The '+ Add signer' affordance is enough to imply the list is editable.

findings.title: Two identical 'Load' rows (vault / request) sit far apart with low affordance
findings.evidence: Desktop shot bottom: 'Load vault' (Vault ID + Load) and 'Load request' (Request ID + Load) are two near-identical input+button rows; the Load buttons are pale/disabled and the two rows are separated by the full create-vault block, making the relationship unclear. They read as leftover utility rows rather than a deliberate 'resume existing' path.
findings.fix: Group the two load rows into one labeled 'Resume / Load' subsection (shared heading) so they read as a pair, and give the disabled Load buttons the same soft-tinted treatment recommended for Create Vault so their state is legible.

verdict: Strong, confident finance UI: gradient hero with three right-aligned stat tiles (TOTAL LOANS / BORROWED / REPAID), a full Borrow card with collateral input, a clear three-up tier selector (Conservative/Balanced/Aggressive), live LTV ratio bar, and a connect-wallet CTA. Desktop and mobile both look polished. The weak spot is the 'ProfitAnchor Vote Route' card consuming primary card weight for static, non-actionable disclosure copy, and an emoji lock in the CTA.
round1_held: Yes. Stat tiles show real 0/0.00 values (correct, not dashes), the 'Pool available' and 'Estimated Borrow (after fee)' rows are present, and the disconnected primary affordance is a clear 'Connect wallet to use Self Loan' bar.

findings.title: 'ProfitAnchor Vote Route' card outranks the actual Borrow interface in the visual hierarchy
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: directly under the hero, a full-width NeoCard titled 'ProfitAnchor Vote Route' shows only a static 'COLLATERAL VOTE SIGNAL / Operator-selected council candidate' label and a 'VOTE-ONLY DEPENDENCY' badge (PlayArea.tsx:287-304). It carries the same card chrome/weight as the Borrow card but is pure non-actionable disclosure, and it pushes the primary Borrow form lower on the page. A first-time user's eye lands on an opaque governance note before the thing they came to do.
findings.fix: Demote this disclosure: render it as a compact inline note/footnote inside or beneath the Borrow card (or a collapsible 'Vote routing' detail) rather than a top-level full-card sibling. Reserve full-card weight for hero + Borrow + Loan Status.

findings.title: Emoji lock glyph in the connect CTA breaks icon consistency
findings.evidence: Desktop shot bottom: the connect bar reads '🔒 Connect wallet to use Self Loan' using an emoji padlock, whereas the rest of the cluster (and this app's hero badge) uses inline stroke SVG icons. The emoji renders at a different weight/baseline than the surrounding text and looks out of place against the Neo Soft icon set.
findings.fix: Replace the 🔒 emoji with an inline lock SVG sized/colored to match (currentColor, ~16px) so the CTA matches the design system's iconography.

findings.title: 'VOTE-ONLY DEPENDENCY' badge label is jargon at first read
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the badge text 'VOTE-ONLY DEPENDENCY' (profitAnchorBadge) in all-caps tracked type is cryptic to a user — it's an internal architectural term, not a user-facing concept, and it's the most prominent text on that card after the value.
findings.fix: Reword to something user-meaningful (e.g. 'Voting only — funds stay in custody') or fold the reassurance into the disclosure copy and drop the badge entirely once the card is demoted per the hierarchy fix.

verdict: Tidy, readable form-first layout: Create Stream card with recipient/amount/duration/notes, a GAS|NEO token segmented control, the two-signature deposit hint, and two empty-state list cards with centered icons and friendly copy. Mobile reflows cleanly. The one clear weakness is the desktop hero collapsing to a thin left-aligned strip with a large empty right half because the summary metrics are hidden at zero streams.
round1_held: Yes. verdict: Clean, focused swap UI with a clear router-unavailable notice and a tidy from/to/detail card; mobile stacks well. findings.title: Exchange rate shown three times (hero RATE, detail EXCHANGE RATE, execute note)

findings.title: Hero RATE box is full-width with the value left-aligned, leaving a large empty void

findings.title: 'Load Listings' primary button shows only a spinner with no label on first paint

findings.title: 'Configure Session Key' primary CTA contrast looks weak in its faded/disabled state on first paint

findings.title: Same first-paint red 'BLOCKED' checklist wall as asset-factory (shared component)

findings.title: 'Royalty bps' helper renders but the relationship between Royalty bps and Max supply column isn't visually grouped

findings.title: 'Needs oracle' / 'Needs OneGate' toggles get less first-paint prominence than the data they gate
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshot bottom: the 'Needs oracle' toggle is an unchecked checkbox in a subtle grey tile, visually the quietest control in the form, yet it materially changes the generated template capability. On the shared form (FactoryPlayArea.tsx:378-381) the two toggles share a row with no description of what enabling oracle does.
findings.fix: Add a one-line sub-label under the miniapp toggles (or a hint prop) explaining the consequence, e.g. 'Oracle capability adds a price/data feed to the generated app.' so the toggle's impact is clear before generating the plan.

verdict: Attractive, restrained search-first console: globe badge + NAME SERVICE eyebrow + title, three stat tiles (0 DOMAINS / 0 EXPIRING / Disconnected WALLET) inline on the right, a prominent search field + green Search button, and a well-crafted empty-state card ('You don't own any domains yet' with centered globe badge + hint). round1_held: Yes. The wallet status tile shows 'Disconnected' as a dot+text indicator (not a fake number), the search-result/owner rows and renew-confirm price disclosure exist in code, em-dash placeholders used (expiry '—'), and the empty state is graceful and content-sized. No regressions.

findings.title: Wallet-status stat tile reads visually lighter/smaller than the two number tiles, breaking the tile row's rhythm
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot hero: 'DOMAINS' and 'EXPIRING' tiles show a bold 18px '0', but the third tile shows 'Disconnected' in 13px text with a small grey dot — so the third tile's primary line sits lower and lighter than its neighbors, making the row feel slightly unbalanced (the eye reads two strong numbers then a faint word). PlayArea.scss:88-92 sets .nns-stat__statusText to 13px/700 vs .nns-stat__value 18px/800.
findings.fix: Either bump .nns-stat__statusText to ~15px and vertically center it to match the numeric tiles' baseline, or visually separate the wallet indicator from the two count tiles (e.g. a thin divider or slightly different bg) so it's read as a status chip rather than a third 'metric' that happens to be undersized.

findings.title: On mobile the 'Search Domain' label floats directly under the stats row with the same gap, so it reads as detached
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshot: stats 3-up row, then the 'Search Domain' label, then the input+Search button. The row-gap between stats and the form label equals the gap inside the hero, so 'Search Domain' visually clings to the stats block above it instead of clearly heading the input below it.
findings.fix: In PlayArea.scss mobile block (@media max-width:640px) add a touch more separation between .nns-hero__stats and the search form (e.g. increase margin-top on .search-row, or move the stats into their own sub-card) so the 'Search Domain' label unambiguously belongs to the input beneath it.

verdict: Polished gradient hero (mint-to-white) with the AA orbit badge, a clear WALLET ACTIONS panel, and carded metric tiles (Your stake / Claimable GAS / Reward reserve / Total staked) — overall a good-looking, well-organized app. BUT the first-paint action panel sends contradictory signals: the anchor input shows a RED invalid border, the primary 'Stake NEO' CTA is disabled-but-tinted-green (looks clickable), and a full-width GREEN 'Ready' status strip sits right below — so the panel simultaneously says 'error', 'go', and 'ready'. Mobile stacks the four action buttons full-width cleanly but inherits the same mixed-signal problem; the orbit badge shows '— AA' which looks like a broken glyph.
round1_held: Partially. Good round-1 work survived: the anchor id is a true placeholder (not a pre-filled fake that could be submitted), the single filled-green primary CTA pattern, em-dash placeholders (Agents: —, Last tx: —), credit-recovery card gated to when there's something to reclaim, and the hover/focus states. HOWEVER the first-paint state still reads as conflicting (red input + disabled-green CTA + green 'Ready' strip) — that messaging coherence wasn't resolved.

findings.title: First-paint shows a green 'Ready' status strip while the form is non-actionable (empty/invalid anchor, disabled CTA, red input border)
findings.evidence: Desktop AND mobile screenshots: the ANCHOR APPID input has a red/pink invalid border (aria-invalid, because anchorInput is the empty placeholder), the 'Stake NEO' primary button is rendered in the soft-green DISABLED state, yet a full-width green strip below reads 'Ready'. statusText resolves to workflowReady='Ready' (PlayArea.tsx:83,32) on first paint even though nothing can be submitted. The hero meanwhile says 'Open an anchor link' / 'Waiting for anchor' — so hero and action strip disagree.
findings.fix: When no valid anchor is entered/linked, make statusText reflect that instead of 'Ready', e.g. show t('anchorAwaitingLaunch')/'Enter or open an anchor link to begin' and render the strip in the neutral (non-green) variant. Only show the green 'Ready' strip once looseAnchorValid (or an anchor is linked). This aligns the strip with the hero and the disabled CTA.

findings.title: Red invalid border on the anchor input at first paint with no inline message
findings.evidence: Desktop/mobile: the ANCHOR APPID field renders with a red border on load (aria-invalid={!anchorInputValid}, PlayArea.tsx:213) because the field is empty showing only the 'custom-anchor:team:nonce' placeholder. A red field on first load — before the user has typed anything — signals 'you made an error' when they haven't, and there's no helper text saying what a valid id looks like.
findings.fix: Only apply aria-invalid / the red border AFTER the user has typed something non-empty (e.g. aria-invalid={anchorInput.length > 0 && !anchorInputValid}, mirroring the pattern already used for the register field at PlayArea.tsx:390). Optionally add a muted format hint under the field ('Format: custom-anchor:team:nonce').

findings.title: Orbit badge displays '— AA' which looks like a broken/placeholder glyph
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile hero: the circular mint orbit badge shows an em-dash on top of 'AA' (displayedAgentCount is '—' before an anchor is linked, PlayArea.tsx:48,192-194). A lone dash centered in a prominent circle reads as missing/erroring data rather than an intentional 'no agents yet' state, undercutting the otherwise premium hero.
findings.fix: Before an anchor is linked, render '0' (with a muted color) or a small AA-cluster icon/glyph in the orbit instead of the bare em-dash, so the badge always looks like a deliberate state. Reserve '—' for inline facts where it reads as 'not applicable', not for the focal hero badge.

verdict: Desktop first paint is clean and professional: white hero with mint shield badge, a 0.00 NEO 'MY STAKE' score block, a 4-up stat row, and a two-column workspace (action card + ROUTE STATE aside). It reads well, but the ROUTE STATE card has an obvious mid-card vertical void and the empty state stacks three muted 'nothing here yet' rows in a row. Mobile shot was not generated, so mobile reflow could not be visually verified.
round1_held: Yes — em-dash placeholder is used for the route-state heading ('—'), the friendly 'No GAS accrued yet' hint and 'Ready for wallet action' status strip render, the recover-credit (exit-path withdraw) card is wired conditionally, and the action history empty state shows 'No wallet action submitted yet.' No regressions seen.

findings.title: ROUTE STATE card has a large empty void between the '—' placeholder and the status rows
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the right ROUTE STATE card shows the eyebrow + a big '—' placeholder at the top, then a wide band of empty mint-tinted space, then Status/Agents/Reward pool/GAS-per-NEO pushed to the very bottom. Code: .anchor-route-card uses align-content:start with min-height:100% (PlayArea.scss:449-453) while its dl has margin-top:auto (PlayArea.scss:485) — the card stretches to match the tall left status card and the auto margin opens a dead zone in the middle.
findings.fix: Remove `margin-top:auto` on `.anchor-route-card dl` (or change `align-content:start` to `space-between` intentionally with a divider) so the status rows sit directly under the placeholder, OR add a small filler (e.g. a one-line route description) between the heading and the dl so the card does not balloon. The cleanest fix is dropping the auto margin so content packs top and the card grows only to its content.

findings.title: Stat chips show '0.00 GAS / 0.00 NEO' on first paint instead of the em-dash placeholder its sibling profitanchor uses
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the 4 stat chips read CLAIMABLE GAS 0.00 GAS, TRACKED NEO 0.00 NEO, REWARD RESERVE 0.00 GAS, CLAIMABLE NEO 0.00 NEO before any data loads. Sibling profitanchor renders '—' for the same not-yet-loaded state (profitanchor PlayArea.tsx:108-127 + .stat-value--placeholder). In trustanchor, main.tsx:54-85 derives every display as `formatNum(0)` with no loaded/placeholder distinction, so a genuine on-chain 0 is indistinguishable from data-not-loaded and the first paint looks like real zeros rather than 'waiting'.
findings.fix: Mirror profitanchor: gate the hero/stat displays on whether `stats` has loaded and render the em-dash placeholder ('—') until then (e.g. `stats ? formatNum(...) : '—'`), matching profitanchor's hasData pattern so the two sibling staking apps paint consistently.

findings.title: Three stacked muted empty rows below the action buttons feel repetitive
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: directly under the button grid there are three consecutive low-emphasis grey rows — 'No GAS accrued yet', a status strip 'Ready for wallet action', and the action-history empty card 'No wallet action submitted yet.' Three near-identical muted blocks in a column dilute the visual hierarchy of the primary Stake action. Source: PlayArea.tsx:225-270.
findings.fix: Collapse the redundancy — e.g. only show the 'No GAS accrued yet' hint when the Claim button is the relevant action, and let the status strip OR the history empty-state carry the 'nothing yet' message rather than both. Reducing to one muted empty cue keeps the Stake CTA visually dominant.

verdict: A genuinely strong operator console: three labelled command cards (Move NEO / Update candidate / Sync vote) on the left, a scrollable 21-agent directory and an Operator-rule safety card on the right, with a clean hero stat strip. Layout, rhythm and density are good on both desktop and mobile. The main blemish is that its hero badge treatment diverges from its sibling profitanchor-admin.
round1_held: Yes — friendly labels and the 'CURRENT VOTE ROUTE None' preview survive, the agent directory shows a populated 21/21 list, and the Operator-rule card with three explicit guarantees renders. Inputs are pre-seeded sensibly. No regressions.

findings.title: Hero badge is a flat outline shield while sibling profitanchor-admin uses a gradient filled icon tile
findings.evidence: trustanchor-admin desktop: the hero badge is a pale mint circle (#e4f8f0) with a thin green outline shield drawn from an inline SVG using currentColor (PlayArea.tsx:125-129, .anchor-admin-hero-badge background var(--anchor-accent-soft), PlayArea.scss:88-97). profitanchor-admin desktop: the badge is a vivid green gradient tile with a solid white up-arrow glyph via the shared <CategoryIcon name="finance"> (profitanchor-admin PlayArea.tsx:93-99). The two sibling admin consoles share the same layout but present two different badge styles.
findings.fix: Pick one badge convention for the admin pair. Either give trustanchor-admin a filled gradient CategoryIcon (e.g. a 'security'/'shield' category icon) to match profitanchor-admin's polish, or downgrade profitanchor-admin to the same flat soft-accent inline glyph. Aligning them removes the family inconsistency.

findings.title: Sync-vote 'Agent' field paints empty while the two sibling forms show pre-filled values
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: Move NEO shows From 1 / To 2, Update candidate shows Agent 1, but the Sync vote Agent input is blank. Code: voteAgentId starts as '' and is only seeded from stats once they load (PlayArea.tsx:40-49); in the standalone/no-stats first paint it stays empty, so the third card looks half-finished next to the two pre-filled cards.
findings.fix: Seed voteAgentId with a sensible default (e.g. '1' or the placeholder shown in CURRENT VOTE ROUTE) until live stats arrive, keeping the voteAgentEdited guard so it still snaps to the on-chain route once data loads. This makes the three command cards paint with consistent example values.

verdict: The most polished of the staking pair: gradient-tinted hero with anchor badge, status pills ('Awaiting route' + '21/21 AA agents registered'), three em-dash stat chips, and a single-column action card with a well-built PREFLIGHT 'Review the wallet effect' panel and a full-width green Stake CTA. Visual hierarchy is clear and it reflows cleanly to mobile. Minor: the preflight left labels are low-contrast and the refresh icon button is easy to miss.
round1_held: Yes — em-dash placeholders on the 3 stat chips, the localized 'Whole NEO amount is ready' inline status, deposit/wallet-effect preflight with the stake memo shown, and the friendly 'Ready for wallet action' status strip all render. No regressions.

findings.title: PREFLIGHT row labels are low-contrast muted grey on the subtle panel background
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: in the PREFLIGHT panel the left-hand labels 'Whole NEO', 'AA route', 'Claimable GAS' are noticeably fainter than their right-hand values. Code: .anchor-preflight-summary dt uses color var(--ns-text-muted) #8a92a6 at 12px (PlayArea.scss:293-297) on a var(--ns-surface-subtle) #f7f8fa panel — roughly a 3.3:1 ratio, under the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text.
findings.fix: Darken the preflight dt labels to var(--ns-text-2) (#5b6478, ~5.7:1) — they are scannable metadata labels, not decorative, so they should clear AA. The values already use --ns-ink so the row stays visually weighted to the right.

findings.title: Refresh action is a small bare icon button that reads like a loading spinner
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: top-right of the WALLET ACTIONS card is a small circular icon-only control that, at a glance, looks like a spinner rather than an affordance. Code: .anchor-refresh-button renders only the refresh SVG with aria-label/title but no visible text (PlayArea.tsx:210-223). Trustanchor by contrast exposes refresh as a labelled 'Refresh status' button.
findings.fix: Either add a visible 'Refresh' text label next to the icon, or give the button a clearer resting affordance (subtle border + hover tooltip is present but the resting state still reads ambiguous). Keeping the icon but adding a small label removes the spinner ambiguity on first paint.

verdict: Clean, dense operator console with a nice touch the sibling lacks: a vivid gradient finance icon tile in the hero and a brand-tinted '21/21' directory header. Three command cards, a 21-agent directory, and an Operator-rule card all render well on desktop; mobile stacks the hero stats into a 2x2 and the Move NEO form reads cleanly. No notable layout defects.
round1_held: Yes — friendly card copy, the 'CURRENT VOTE ROUTE None' preview, pre-seeded inputs, the agent directory and the three-guarantee safety list all render correctly. No regressions.

findings.title: Hero badge / directory-header accent treatment diverges from sibling trustanchor-admin
findings.evidence: profitanchor-admin desktop shows a saturated green gradient icon tile with a white up-arrow (CategoryIcon name="finance", PlayArea.tsx:93-99) and a green-tinted directory heading; trustanchor-admin desktop shows a flat pale-mint outline shield and a plain heading. Same admin layout, two different visual identities. (Counterpart finding logged on trustanchor-admin.)
findings.fix: Align the pair on one badge/header convention — see the trustanchor-admin finding. No change needed in profitanchor-admin if trustanchor-admin is upgraded to match; otherwise normalize both to the same treatment.

verdict: Looks great and purposeful: gradient hero with a fingerprint badge and three metric tiles (Network / Resolver / Passports 0), a clear numbered 3-step route bar (Resolve DID / Build credential / Optional wallet proof), and a two-column workspace with a tidy form on the left and a centered 'Awaiting DID resolution' empty card on the right. Mobile stacks the hero, metrics and steps vertically with good spacing. This is a strong, demanding-designer-approved first paint.
round1_held: Yes — em-dash/friendly empty state ('Awaiting DID resolution' with icon + helper copy), the 'Not signed' proof-status chip, localized alert lane, the disabled Sign Passport CTA (correctly inactive until a payload is built), and the degraded-runtime warning path all survive. No regressions.

findings.title: Left form column leaves a tall empty gap below the Reset button because the result panel is taller
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the form column ends at the 'Reset' link while the right result/empty panel (min-height 360px) extends much lower, leaving a visible blank band below the left column. Code: .neodid-passport__workspace uses align-items:start (PlayArea.scss:179) with the empty result panel at min-height:360px (PlayArea.scss:451). The asymmetry is expected behavior, but the void on the left is noticeable on a wide viewport.
findings.fix: Optional polish only: this is acceptable as-is (form should not stretch). If tightening is desired, reduce the empty-result min-height a touch (e.g. 300px) or anchor the empty card's vertical centering to the form height so the columns feel more balanced. Low priority — the empty state itself is well composed.

verdict: Clean, legible compose form with a nice recipient-only/time-locked toggle and correct disconnected empty states. But the hero is the plainest in the cluster — bare text with no icon badge or eyebrow — and the 'Network: No EVM wallet detected' notice reads like body copy rather than a warning, so the first paint feels flatter and less branded than its siblings (private-transfer, soulbound, sign-anything all lead with an icon tile).
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders, friendly empty states ('Connect your wallet to view your messages.'), localized network/error copy, and the byte counter (0/2000) all render correctly. No regressions.

findings.title: Hero lacks the icon badge + eyebrow every sibling app has
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile shots: the neo-message hero is just an H2 'Encrypted & time-locked messages' over a gray subtitle, with no leading icon tile or uppercase eyebrow. Every other privacy-cluster app (private-transfer 'NEO N3 PRIVATE PAYMENTS' + lock tile, soulbound 'ISSUER WORKSPACE' + glyph, sign-anything 'WALLET-REVIEWED PROOF DESK' + pen tile, recovery-guardian shield tile + 'RECOVERY GUARDIAN') leads with a colored icon badge and eyebrow. PlayArea.tsx:130-133 renders only nm-hero-title + nm-hero-sub.
findings.fix: Add a 40-48px rounded accent badge (lock/envelope SVG in the app's #5b6ef5 accent) and an uppercase eyebrow (e.g. 'CONFIDENTIAL MESSAGING') above the H2 in .nm-hero, matching the sibling hero pattern. Wrap title+sub in a copy column beside the badge.

findings.title: 'No EVM wallet' network notice has no warning affordance
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the 'Network' card body 'No EVM wallet detected. Install MetaMask…' is rendered in the same muted gray as ordinary helper text inside a plain white card — nothing signals it is a blocking precondition. PlayArea.tsx:136-138 uses a neutral NeoCard + .nm-network-warning which in PlayArea.scss:47-51 is just colored text, no border/background/icon.
findings.fix: Give .nm-network-warning a soft warning treatment (amber-tinted background like #fff4e5 with a small alert icon and an accent left border) so the disconnected/unsupported state reads as an action item, not body copy. The badge colors #fff4e5/#c47d18 already exist in this stylesheet for the 'locked' badge.

findings.title: Note box muted text contrast is borderline
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the privacy note under the mode toggle ('The message is encrypted to the oracle key and stored on-chain…') is very faint gray on a light gray fill. PlayArea.scss:141-149 sets color var --ns-text-faint #8a8fa0 on background #f6f7fb — roughly 3.2:1, under the 4.5:1 WCAG AA threshold for this 12px body text.
findings.fix: Bump the note text to --ns-text-muted (#6b7180) which clears AA on the #f6f7fb fill, keeping it visually secondary without dropping below the contrast floor.

verdict: The strongest-looking app in the cluster: branded hero with lock tile + eyebrow + green 'No on-chain zk curve dependency' badge, a balanced single-column form (grid--solo before sealing), tidy preset pills, and a clean numbered 4-step explainer. Desktop and mobile both read well. The 'Mainnet · Degraded' default correctly surfaces the live oracle outage.
round1_held: Yes. Network health badging (Degraded), em-dash/digest placeholders, validation hint dot ('Add a valid recipient and positive amount…'), and the disabled seal button all render as intended. No regressions.

findings.title: Sealed-intents empty state is a lone centered line inside a tall card
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the 'SEALED INTENTS' card shows only the single dashed line 'Sealed transfer intents will appear here after you seal one.' with generous padding above/below, leaving the card feeling empty next to the dense form above it. PlayArea.tsx:645-647 renders .private-transfer__history-empty as a bare dashed box.
findings.fix: Add a small monochrome icon (a 'receipt'/lock glyph in the accent-soft tile already used by the hero/steps) above the empty text and tighten vertical padding, so the empty state matches the polish of the step cards rather than reading as dead space.

findings.title: Network shown as 'Degraded' with no inline explanation in the select
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the Network select reads 'Mainnet · Degraded' but nothing on first paint tells the user what Degraded means or that sealing may fail. The hero badge instead advertises 'No on-chain zk curve dependency' (a positive), so the only health signal is the terse select suffix from PlayArea.tsx:451-456.
findings.fix: When the selected network resolves to 'degraded', render a one-line inline hint under the select (reusing the existing __validation pill styling) such as 'Oracle key unavailable on this network — sealing is paused.' so the state is self-explanatory rather than a cryptic suffix.

verdict: Information-dense but coherent: shield-badge hero with three em-dash metric tiles, a 01/02/03 flow strip, a 'Recovery state' panel with a proper search-icon empty state, and a 'Prepare Recovery' side rail. It holds together, but the side rail is heavy (form + 6 link buttons) and one badge uses a placeholder-looking 'SR' text glyph. Mobile reflows cleanly to a single column.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders in metric tiles (Account/New Owner '—', Expiry '30'), the 'Enter a valid account address or Hash160 before querying state.' guard hint, and the 'Awaiting query' idle pill all render correctly. No regressions.

findings.title: Risk-note badge uses a literal 'SR' text glyph that looks like a placeholder
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the bottom risk note in the Recovery-state panel shows a green rounded tile containing the two letters 'SR' next to the safety copy. PlayArea.tsx:260-261 hardcodes SR; every other badge/tile in the app uses a proper SVG icon (shield, search). The bare initials read as an unfinished avatar stub, not an icon.
findings.fix: Replace the 'SR' text with an inline SVG (a shield/alert glyph consistent with the hero shield) inside .guardian-risk-note > span, or drop the tile and use a small warning icon — so the note matches the iconography used everywhere else in the app.

findings.title: Prepare-Recovery side rail packs six identical secondary buttons in a 2x3 grid
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: under the form the side rail shows six look-alike buttons (Open/Copy/Share Recovery Preview + Open/Copy/Share Recovery Credential) in a uniform grid with no grouping, making it hard to distinguish 'preview' from 'credential' actions at a glance. PlayArea.tsx:98-105 + 321-333 render all six in one .guardian-link-grid.
findings.fix: Split into two labeled subgroups ('Recovery preview' / 'Recovery credential'), each a row of Open/Copy/Share, and visually distinguish the primary 'Open' from the Copy/Share utilities (e.g. Open filled-soft, Copy/Share as compact icon buttons) to reduce the wall-of-buttons feel.

findings.title: Hero/flow/workspace breakpoints collapse at 960px but desktop side rail can feel cramped between
findings.evidence: Desktop shot at full width: the workspace right column min is 360px (PlayArea.scss:272 minmax(360px, 440px)) while it must hold a form with four inputs plus the six-button grid; the buttons' labels ('Open Recovery Credential') nearly fill their cells. At intermediate widths just above 960px this column is tightest before the single-column fallback kicks in.
findings.fix: Lower the link-grid to a single column when the side rail is under ~400px (a container/width query or an added 760-960px breakpoint), so the longer button labels never truncate or wrap awkwardly between the 960px collapse and full desktop.

verdict: Polished two-panel signing desk — Message composer + Proof output side by side, a collapsible flow disclosure, and a right 'Transaction safety' rail with a clear Disconnected pill. The composer and proof cards look great. The one real eyesore is the desktop right column: the 'Transaction safety' card is short and the column beneath it is a large void because the layout aligns to the top instead of filling.
round1_held: Yes. Disconnected status pill, 'No signature yet'/'No broadcast yet' empty states with disabled copy buttons, the local-hash file notice, and the 'wallet prompt opens when you sign' reassurance all render correctly. No regressions.

findings.title: Desktop right column is mostly empty under the short 'Transaction safety' card
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the right rail holds only the 'Transaction safety' card (header + two lines + a collapsed 'On-chain broadcast' disclosure), ending around y=250, while the left column runs to y=830 — leaving ~580px of blank canvas in the right column. PlayArea.scss:33-39 sets .sign-shell to a 2-col grid with align-items: start, so the short aside does not stretch and the gap is left bare.
findings.fix: Either expand the safety rail to fill (move the broadcast details inline/expanded, or surface the sign/broadcast route + 0 GAS + privacy rows that are currently hidden inside the <details> so the card has real height), or drop to a single-column stacked layout on desktop so the proof output sits directly under the composer with no dead column.

findings.title: Proof output panel sits empty beside a much taller composer
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: 'Proof output' shows only two short empty boxes ('No signature yet', 'No broadcast yet') and the panel bottom is blank from ~y=560 down to y=830, mirroring the composer's height only because of the card border. The first-paint balance is composer-heavy, proof-empty.
findings.fix: Give the empty Proof output a centered placeholder illustration/icon + one explanatory line ('Sign or broadcast a message to see its proof here.') vertically centered, so the empty panel reads as intentional rather than two stranded boxes at the top.

verdict: Feature-rich issuer workspace that looks professional — green gradient identity badge, two-column workspace, a friendly robot 'Wallet not connected' illustration in Your Templates, and a complete Create Template form. The weakness is vertical balance on desktop: the left column's 'Issue Certificate' card is tall with a big empty stretch under the Issue button before 'Verify'/'My Certificates', so the two columns are noticeably uneven.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders, friendly empty states ('Certificates issued to this wallet will appear here.', 'Connect a wallet to load your certificate templates.'), the disabled Issue/Lookup buttons, and the robot illustration empty state all render correctly. No regressions.

findings.title: Uneven column heights leave a large white gap in the left workspace column
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the left column shows 'Issue Certificate' (ends ~y=1010) then 'Verify' then 'My Certificates', while the right column 'Your Templates' + 'Create Template' ends ~y=1010 — but the Issue card itself carries a tall empty stretch below its Issue button before Verify begins, and 'My Certificates' (a single empty line) trails far down at ~y=1430 with the right column already finished. The 2-col grid (PlayArea.scss:204-208, align-items: start) lets the columns drift out of balance.
findings.fix: Rebalance the masonry: move 'Verify' and/or 'My Certificates' into the right column under 'Create Template' (or use a 3-stack distribution) so neither column has a long empty tail. Alternatively cap the Issue card height and let the disconnected state fill it, removing the gap between Issue and Verify.

findings.title: Disabled Issue / Lookup buttons render as washed pale-green text with weak contrast
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the disconnected-state 'Issue' button (pale mint fill, faint green label) and the 'Lookup' button read as very low-contrast — the green-on-mint label is hard to see and gives little signal that it is intentionally disabled vs. broken. These are the primary NeoButtons at PlayArea.tsx:370-378 / 485-492 in their disabled state.
findings.fix: Style the disabled primary state with a neutral gray fill + gray label (clearing ~4.5:1) instead of pale-green-on-mint, so disabled reads unambiguously and the label stays legible; keep the green only for the enabled/active state.

findings.title: Left 'Selected template' chooser and Template-ID input are redundant on first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: the Issue panel shows a 'SELECTED TEMPLATE — Choose a template or enter an ID' strip, then a greyed 'Connect a wallet to load your certificate templates.' box, then a 'Template ID' input prefilled '1' — three stacked ways to specify the same template before anything is connected, which is a lot of redundant UI for the empty state. Driven by PlayArea.tsx:282-328 (selected-template + template-picker + templateId field).
findings.fix: In the disconnected/empty state, collapse to just the Template ID input (the picker has nothing to show anyway) and reveal the 'Selected template' summary strip only once a template is actually picked, reducing the empty-state clutter.

verdict: Genuinely strong: a clean white hero with eyebrow/title/subtitle, three pill flow-steps, a wallet status card with a real Connect Wallet button, and a well-balanced two-column create/events workspace. The full-width Issue/Check-in desk and My Tickets panels read clearly even empty. The one real visual flaw is the disabled 'Issue' CTA rendering as a fully-saturated green bar that looks clickable.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders (short() returns '—'), localized workflow status ('Ready'), wallet-not-connected label, friendly empty states with icons, and the staleness guard that clears a prior lookup when the check-in token id changes are all present and rendering correctly in the screenshots.

findings.title: Disabled primary CTAs ('Issue', transfer) stay solid green and read as enabled
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the 'Issue' button under the Issue Ticket form is a full-width, fully-saturated bright-green bar identical to an enabled CTA, yet with no event selected and no recipient it is disabled (PlayArea.tsx:334 disabled={!canIssueTicket}). The cause: PlayArea.scss:634 `.ticket-play-area .neo-btn--primary{background:var(--tk-accent)}` has higher specificity than the shared `.neo-btn:disabled` grey reset (NeoButton.scss:25), so disabled primaries keep the green fill. Sibling apps timestamp-proof and graveyard explicitly add a soft-green :disabled tint; this app does not, so it's inconsistent and the affordance is misleading.
findings.fix: Add a disabled rule mirroring the siblings, e.g. in PlayArea.scss: `.ticket-play-area .neo-btn--primary:disabled{background:var(--tk-accent-soft);color:var(--tk-accent-strong);box-shadow:none;opacity:.85;}` so the disabled Issue/Transfer CTAs read as a soft, non-clickable state.

findings.title: Hero subtitle/body has no text below it, leaving the left hero column visually top-heavy
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the hero left column ends right after the three flow pills, while the right wallet card + Connect button sits noticeably lower, so the two hero columns have unequal visual mass with empty space under the flow pills. The grid is `align-items: stretch` (PlayArea.scss:27) but the content doesn't fill the height.
findings.fix: Minor; either vertically center the wallet side (`.ticket-hero__side{justify-content:center}`) or let the flow-pill row anchor to the bottom of the copy column so both columns terminate at a similar baseline.

verdict: Clean and centered at max-width 760px so the desktop canvas doesn't feel empty. Hero card, three stat tiles (0/0/—), Create and Verify cards, and a friendly 'No proofs yet' empty state with an accent badge all render well. The one jarring thing is the duplicated 'Enter content to timestamp' string and the soft-green disabled Create button which together look like a half-broken control.
round1_held: Yes. The em-dash for Latest ID (PlayArea.tsx:30 maps 'N/A'/empty to '—'), soft-green disabled CTA tint (PlayArea.scss:79), input-preserved-on-failure create handler, and verify-error clearing are all present and visible.

findings.title: 'Enter content to timestamp' is shown twice — as the textarea label and again as a hint under the button
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the textarea is labelled 'Enter content to timestamp', and directly under the (disabled) Create Proof button the exact same sentence 'Enter content to timestamp' is repeated as bold helper text. Reading the identical phrase twice within one card looks like a bug, not guidance.
findings.fix: Give the hint its own copy that says why the button is disabled, e.g. a new key like 'createDisabledHint' = 'Add some text above to enable timestamping', instead of reusing t('enterContent') at PlayArea.tsx:92.

findings.title: Disabled Create button hint sits centered and floats with no anchoring to the input
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the soft-green disabled 'Create Proof' button plus the centered hint below create a stack of three center-aligned green-tinted elements (textarea border, button, hint) that reads slightly unbalanced against the left-aligned label above. The hint (PlayArea.scss:88 text-align:center) doesn't match the left-aligned field label rhythm.
findings.fix: If keeping the hint, left-align it under the field or attach it as the NeoInput hint prop so it sits with the input rather than below the CTA.

verdict: The hero is attractive (gradient wash, icon badge, clear 3-step timeline) and the 4-tile vault strip is clean. The weak spot is the 'Memory upload' card's internal two-column layout: a nested 'Album' sub-card (empty, very short) on the left next to a much taller 'Choose images' uploader on the right, producing a lopsided grid with a large empty gap under the Album card and a redundant card-inside-a-card frame.
round1_held: Yes. Localized upload readiness states (passwordRequired/totalTooLarge/readyToSave), the upload error alert block, the size meter, em-dash-free byte formatting, and the local-storage note are all present and the bound limit now reads from maxTotalBytes (PlayArea.tsx:69).

findings.title: Lopsided columns inside 'Memory upload': short empty Album card vs tall uploader leaves a big empty gap
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: inside the 'Memory upload' card the left 'Album' sub-card shows only the one-line empty placeholder ('No photos yet · Save your first memory…') and ends high up, while the right 'Choose images' column (dropzone + 0/60KB + encrypt toggle + note) is roughly 2x taller, so the bottom-left quadrant is a large blank void. Grid defined at PlayArea.scss:230 `grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(280px,0.62fr); align-items:start`.
findings.fix: Either make the Album card span full width above the uploader when empty (stack instead of side-by-side until there are photos), or give the empty AlbumGrid a min-height that matches the uploader column so the two columns terminate together.

findings.title: Card-inside-a-card: 'Album' NeoCard nested inside the 'Memory upload' NeoCard reads as double-framing
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: 'Memory upload' is a white bordered card; immediately inside it the AlbumGrid renders another titled white card ('Album') with its own border/shadow (AlbumGrid.tsx:21 NeoCard title=albumTab; AlbumGrid.scss adds border + shadow). Two stacked card chromes inside one card looks heavier than the flat right-hand uploader panel, and the 'Album' title duplicates the section's intent.
findings.fix: Render the album area as a plain panel (drop the inner NeoCard border/shadow, keep just the gallery/empty content) so there's a single card frame around the upload workspace.

verdict: Solid and atmospheric: tombstone icon badge, R.I.P eyebrow, three hero stat tiles, a two-column Burial Chamber / Burial Records layout, a clear write/hash toggle, tag chips, and a red 'Permanent record' warning. align-self:start correctly stops the empty Records card from stretching. round1_held: Yes. The soft-green disabled burial CTA (PlayArea.scss:488 .destroy-form .neo-btn--primary:disabled tints brand-soft), the danger warning note, the local-hash preview, and the friendly 'No burial records yet' empty state with icon are all present and visible.

findings.title: Right column 'Burial Records' empty card is much shorter than the tall left chamber, leaving a long blank right rail
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the left 'Burial Chamber' card runs the full height (toggle + textarea + tags + warning + CTA) while the right 'Burial Records' card is a short box with just the empty-state icon and 'No burial records yet', so the entire lower-right area of the canvas is empty. Grid is two equal columns (PlayArea.scss:130-135) with align-self:start, so the right card floats at the top.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is, but to balance the first paint consider giving the empty records card a taller min-height (~the chamber's) or adding a short helper line under 'No burial records yet' (e.g. 'Buried memories will appear here.') so the right column isn't a near-empty box.

findings.title: 'Refresh Records' control is plain low-contrast text with no button affordance
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: in the Burial Records header, 'Refresh Records' sits as muted grey text next to a small '0' count chip, with no border, icon, or fill — it doesn't read as an interactive control compared to the clearly-styled buttons elsewhere in the app.
findings.fix: Give the refresh action a ghost-button treatment with a refresh icon (matching event-ticket-pass's 'REFRESH' ghost buttons) so it reads as clickable.

verdict: The hero is well composed — heart badge, MEMORIALS eyebrow, title, subtitle, a green Create Memorial CTA, and a clean 4-tile stat strip. But the empty first paint is weak on desktop: the hero + a single wide, ultra-short 'No memorials yet' card occupy only the top ~35% of the canvas, leaving a very large blank area below that makes the page feel unfinished.
round1_held: Yes. Stats show clean 0s, the dashed em-style empty card with italic 'No memorials yet. Create the first one above.' is present (PlayArea.tsx:340), inline year validation and the chain-receipt block are coded, and the single green accent hue is consistent.

findings.title: Empty-state desktop first paint is top-heavy: tiny one-line empty card under the hero with a huge blank canvas below
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: after the hero card, the only other element is a wide, very short dashed card containing a single italic line 'No memorials yet. Create the first one above.'; everything sits in the top third and the lower ~65% of the frame is empty white. The empty card (.empty-memorials, PlayArea.scss:471) has padding 40px/20px but no min-height and no illustration/icon, so it collapses to one text line and looks unbalanced.

findings.title: Empty memorials card lacks the inline create affordance the copy promises
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the empty card says 'Create the first one above.' pointing back up at the hero's Create Memorial button, but the card itself has no action — unlike graveyard/forever-album/event-ticket empty states which place a button right in the empty zone. The eye has to travel back up to the hero.
findings.fix: Add a small secondary 'Create Memorial' button inside .empty-memorials that calls the same setShowCreateForm(true), so the empty state is self-contained like the sibling apps.

verdict: Clean, calm two-column form. The left create-capsule form is genuinely nicely laid out; round-1 deposit/storage notes and em-dash placeholders are present. The main rendered flaw is a badly unbalanced desktop grid: the right column (Fish + Your Capsules) is short and the empty 'No capsules yet' card leaves a large white void at bottom-right while the left form runs much longer.
round1_held: Yes. Refundable-deposit note ('The 0.2 GAS is a refundable deposit... not a spent fee'), local-storage note, friendly empty state, and disabled CTA soft-tint all present and visible in the screenshot.

findings.title: Desktop columns badly unbalanced — tall form vs short right stack leaves a large empty void
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: left 'Create New Capsule' card runs from ~y240 down past y900 to the CTA, while the right column ('Fish a Capsule' ~y245-410 + 'Your Capsules' ~y440-665) ends at ~y665, leaving roughly 250px of blank canvas under the right column. The two columns terminate at very different heights, making the page look top-heavy on the right.
findings.fix: In PlayArea.scss the desktop grid is minmax(0,1.15fr)/minmax(320px,0.85fr). Either (a) make the right .capsule-side-panel align-self:stretch and let 'Your Capsules' min-height grow to fill, or (b) move 'Fish a Capsule' to sit beside the hero / reduce the right column to a single sticky panel. findings.title: Empty 'Your Capsules' state is a bare tinted circle with no icon or CTA
findings.evidence: Desktop + the CapsuleList empty render: a plain pale-green filled circle sits above 'No capsules yet. Create your first one!' with no glyph inside the circle and no affordance — it reads as a loading placeholder rather than an intentional empty illustration.
findings.fix: In components/CapsuleList give the empty-state circle a lock/capsule SVG glyph (matching the unbreakable-vault empty-state which uses a lock icon) so the empty state looks designed, not mid-load.

verdict: Hero and create form look sharp. The weak spot is the stat row: the two stat tiles render as a bare big number + tiny caption floating inside full-width white cards with almost no visual weight, so 'MY VAULTS / OPEN VAULTS' read like stray text rather than metric tiles — noticeably less polished than the boxed stat tiles in sibling apps (time-capsule, daily-checkin). Right column also ends well above the left, leaving empty space.
round1_held: Yes. Secret/confirm-secret with mismatch guard, min-bounty note, 'Secret is hashed locally...' note, soft-tinted disabled CTA, and the lock-icon 'No vaults found' empty state are all present.

findings.title: Stat tiles read as floating text, not tiles — number left-aligned in an oversized empty white card

Either constrain the .vault-stats grid width / center it, or restyle .vault-stat with a subtle surface-subtle background + accent number treatment like daily-checkin's .checkin-stat-item, and reduce the tile width so the number and label aren't stranded against a wide blank.

findings.title: Right column (Break + Recent Vaults) ends far above the tall Create form, leaving a blank lower-right

Consider letting the Recent Vaults panel grow (min-height) or stacking the right column under a sticky position so the void reads intentional; alternatively move Recent Vaults to a full-width row beneath the two-column block.

verdict: Information-rich and mostly well composed — the streak hero, week tracker, Today Plan, milestone ladder and global stats all render cleanly. But the primary action card is broken-looking on first paint: two of the three action buttons show only a bare loading spinner with NO label, flanking the single labeled 'Claim Rewards (0 GAS)' button, so the most important control on the screen looks half-rendered.
round1_held: Yes for content — friendly Today-Plan copy, em-dash-free zero states, milestone ladder, evidence accordion, 'Best: 0 Days' all present. But the round-1 disabled-CTA soft-tint fix is undermined visually because the buttons are stuck in loading (spinner) state, not disabled-tinted state, at first paint.

findings.title: Action card shows two unlabeled spinner buttons flanking Claim Rewards on first paint — looks half-loaded
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile shots: the action card (the green-tinted card after the week tracker) renders three slots as [spinner] [Claim Rewards (0 GAS)] [spinner] — the left check-in button and the right refresh button display only a centered loader with no text. PlayArea.tsx passes loading={isLoading} to both the check-in NeoButton (line ~190) and the refresh NeoButton (line ~213), and isLoading is true while the first chain read is in flight, so both labels are replaced by spinners while the hero pill also says 'Loading…'.
findings.fix: Don't put the check-in and refresh buttons into spinner state for the initial status load. Gate their `loading` on action-specific flags (e.g. a separate isCheckingIn / isRefreshing) rather than the global isLoading, OR while !hasLoadedStatus render them disabled with their text label ('Check in' / 'Refresh') instead of loading={isLoading}. The text label should never disappear during background hydration.

findings.title: Three-button action grid (1fr 1fr auto) makes Refresh a cramped icon-only-feeling third column
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr) auto means the refresh button (3rd col) is much narrower than the other two; with its label hidden by the spinner it collapses to a tiny ~50px pill at the right edge, visually orphaned from the two wide buttons.
findings.fix: Either give the refresh button equal width (3 equal columns) or move it out of the primary action row entirely (e.g. a small text/icon 'Refresh' link in the card header, mirroring automation-copilot's header Refresh), so the primary row is just Check-in + Claim at full width.

verdict: The most polished of this cluster. Green-accent console reads cleanly: gradient hero, paired Neo N3 <-> Neo X chain cards, route summary strip, Asset/Message/Track segmented control, amount + destination form, and footer doc links all render crisply on both desktop and mobile. No broken or empty-looking regions.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders for unset DIGEST/AMOUNT/RECIPIENT are present and correct (lastDigest defaults to '—', confirmed in PlayArea.tsx line 97-101); the route summary shows 'Neo N3 -> Neo X' with clean dashes.

findings.title: Route-summary strip has four columns but two are filled and two are em-dashes, leaving the right half looking empty before input
