findings.fix: Optional: drop the DIGEST column from the top hero strip until a handoff is prepared (it only becomes meaningful post-prepare), or merge the two route summaries so 'Neo N3 -> Neo X' isn't repeated twice on first paint. Not a defect, just a redundancy/empty-column tightening.

verdict: Clean, professional console. Two-column layout (Recipe Builder left, Trigger Status + numbered Automation Route right) is balanced and the green 'Register Trigger' CTA is the clear primary. Selects, schedule presets (Hourly/Every 6h/Daily), and the empty Trigger Status state with power-icon + 'Register or refresh a trigger...' all render well on desktop and mobile.
round1_held: Yes. The honest gateway-fallback note ('Gateway fallbacks are labeled as handoff intents, not successful triggers') is present and the empty Trigger Status uses a friendly icon + copy, not a bare spinner.

findings.title: Collapsed 'Payload' card sits alone at the bottom with empty canvas below it on desktop
findings.evidence: Desktop shot: after the two-column block ends (~y730), the full-width 'Payload ... DETAILS v' card appears at ~y790 as a thin collapsed strip, and below it is empty page to the bottom edge (~y870). The collapsed payload bar floating under the much taller two-column block reads as a slightly orphaned footer.

verdict: Clean, well-organized first paint: a calm hero with N3 badge, a prominent search card with a real Mainnet/Testnet pill toggle, a tidy 4-up metrics strip and a recent-tx empty state. Desktop looks professional; mobile reflows correctly with the toggle stacking. The weak spots are all in the resting/empty state — four em-dash tiles plus a bare-label empty card read a touch sparse, and the disabled Search button is very low-contrast.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash placeholders are present across the metrics strip and recent-tx tiles (PENDING_PLACEHOLDER, is-pending styling), the inline 'Please enter a search query' hint renders under the search box, and the recent-transactions empty-state guidance card survives. No regressions visible.

findings.title: Disabled Search button is near-invisible — looks broken, not disabled
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the full-width 'Search' button below the input renders as light-gray text on a near-white fill — the label barely reads and the button looks like an empty bar rather than a deliberately disabled CTA. This is the first-paint state (empty query), so it is the first thing a user sees under the search field.
findings.fix: In SearchPanel.scss give the disabled primary search button a clearer resting treatment (e.g. a subtle filled surface --ns-surface-subtle with --ns-text-2 label and a 1px border) so it reads as a real, intentionally-inactive control. Alternatively darken the disabled label to meet ~4.5:1 against the fill.

findings.title: Recent-transactions empty state shows three bare word-pills with no instruction
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot, bottom card: left column reads 'NO RECENT TRANSACTIONS LOADED / Run a search or refresh chain data...', and the right column is three gray boxes containing only 'Tx hash', 'Address', 'Contract' (locale keys explorerTipTx/Address/Contract in messages.ts are single words). With no leading label like 'You can look up:' they look like inert chips rather than guidance on what is searchable.
findings.fix: In RecentTransactions.tsx add a small eyebrow above the <ul> (e.g. t('explorerSearchableTypes') = 'Search by') so the three pills read as a captioned 'searchable types' list, or expand each locale string to a short phrase ('Transaction hash', 'Account address', 'Contract hash').

findings.title: First-paint metrics strip is four identical em-dash tiles — low information scent
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: BLOCK HEIGHT, TRANSACTIONS, RECENT TXS, SEARCH RESULT all show the same '—'. Four uppercase labels over four identical dashes reads flat and gives no sense the explorer is live before data lands.
findings.fix: Acceptable as a standalone empty state, but the strip would feel more alive if the live BLOCK HEIGHT / TRANSACTIONS figures (mainnetHeight/mainnetTxCount already fetched on mount via loadAll) were not also collapsed to '—' by isPendingFigure treating '0' as pending. Consider only collapsing truly-absent ('N/A') values so real chain figures show on first paint when the standalone fetch succeeds.

verdict: The two cards (hero with Generate action + Convert Key) are clean and the green primary buttons read well, but the page is short — content ends around 450px and the bottom ~55% of the desktop viewport is empty white space, making the tool feel unfinished/floating. Mobile is well-proportioned. The hero stat tiles (0 ACCOUNTS / — / —) are a sensible empty state.
round1_held: Yes. The em-dash balance placeholders are present (BALANCE_PLACEHOLDER for NEO/GAS when disconnected), the 'Connect a wallet to see live NEO / GAS balances' note renders, and the masked-secret / reveal flow is intact in code. No regressions visible.

findings.title: Large dead vertical space below the Convert Key card on desktop
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: both cards stack in the top ~450px and everything below (roughly half the visible canvas) is blank white. With only two short cards the tool looks sparse and bottom-heavy-empty, unlike sibling tools (treasury, wallet-health) that fill the column.
findings.fix: Fill the resting state with purposeful content: e.g. a compact 'What you can paste' card (WIF / private key / public key / NeoVM script chips with one-line descriptions), or move the disassembler/opcode hint into a visible info card. Even a short security note ('Keys are generated and converted entirely on-device; nothing leaves your browser') as a styled card would balance the column and reinforce trust.

findings.title: Hero stat tiles repeat the connect message that is also stated just below
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the three hero stats show '0 ACCOUNTS / — NEO BALANCE / — GAS BALANCE' and immediately beneath them the line 'Connect a wallet to see live NEO / GAS balances.' The two dash tiles plus the note say the same thing twice in the same card.
findings.fix: Either drop the two balance tiles until a wallet is connected (showing only ACCOUNTS in the disconnected state and revealing NEO/GAS on connect), or remove the redundant note and rely on the em-dash tiles + a tooltip. Avoid stating 'no balance' in two adjacent forms.

verdict: Strong, dense dashboard: hero with live-synced signal + three big USD/NEO/GAS metrics reads professional, the disbursement console is thorough, and the two-column Da Hongfei / Erik Zhang watchlist at the bottom is information-rich. Desktop looks like a real treasury tool. Mobile stacks cleanly. Main concern is the disbursement form is long and a few label/heading rhythms compete for attention.
round1_held: Yes. The 'Live balances synced · Last updated 6/13/2026' signal with green dot renders, em-dash placeholders are used for failed/absent figures (formatUsd, wallet.failed), the review panel and collapsible intent panel are present, and stale/price-feed warnings are wired. No regressions visible.

findings.title: Disbursement console is a tall stack of same-weight panels with no visual priority
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: under 'Disbursement console' the wallet/network/status strip, the asset+amount+recipient+memo form, the preset chips, the review panel, and the collapsible intent panel all sit as full-width same-color sub-cards. The eye has no anchor — it is a long uniform ladder before reaching the Connect / Submit buttons.
findings.fix: Tighten hierarchy: the read-only wallet/network/status strip and the review panel are both summaries of the same draft — consider merging or making the review panel visually secondary (smaller, muted) so the editable form is clearly the primary block. Reducing one redundant summary row would shorten the form noticeably.

findings.title: Hero copy column and metrics column are visually unbalanced on desktop
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the left hero copy block (badge + title + description + signal line) is fairly short while the right metrics column has three tall stacked tiles; the right column visually outweighs and ends lower than the left, leaving the left side with trailing empty space below the signal line.
findings.fix: Either vertically center the hero copy against the metrics (align-content already center on .treasury-hero__copy — but the grid align-items: stretch makes the copy column stretch), or move the failedCount/priceFeed warnings and a one-line 'watching N addresses across 2 groups' summary into the copy block to fill the gap and balance heights.

verdict: The best-looking of the four: a two-column layout (main + sticky safety checklist) that fills the canvas, a conic-gradient score ring, a clean balance strip, and a well-structured 6-item checklist with per-item action buttons. Desktop reads polished and product-grade; mobile stacks the checklist below correctly. The 'High risk / score 0' empty state is honestly the correct disconnected state and looks intentional.
round1_held: Yes. Em-dash NEO/GAS placeholders render when disconnected, the 'Connect a Neo N3 wallet to refresh live balances...' hint is present, the report-status aria-live line ('Report ready') shows, and the auto-check item correctly shows 'Connect to check'. No regressions visible.

findings.title: Score ring shows a bare '0' that reads as a loading/error glyph at first paint
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile screenshots: the hero ring renders a lone '0' with an almost-empty green track. Disconnected, the safety score genuinely is 0, but a stark '0' in a near-empty ring next to a red 'High risk' chip can read as a broken/empty meter rather than 'connect to compute your score'.
findings.fix: When disconnected (isConnected false / safetyScore 0 with no completed checklist), render the ring with a muted '—' or a small 'Connect' affordance instead of a literal 0, or add a one-line caption under the ring ('Connect to score'). The checklist already drives a real local score, so the 0 is only momentarily meaningful.

findings.title: Two 'Mark done' buttons and one 'Connect to check' pill differ in style mid-list, creating a slight rhythm break
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot, safety checklist: item 2 (Keep GAS for fees) shows a green-dotted 'Connect to check' pill while items 1,3,4,5,6 show outlined 'Mark done' buttons. The single differently-styled row in the middle of an otherwise uniform list draws the eye and can read as the odd-one-out rather than an intentional auto-checked item.
findings.fix: This is intentional (auto item) and acceptable, but align the auto pill's height/width and corner radius exactly to the Mark done buttons (it uses min-width 96px / min-height 32px vs the buttons' 96px — verify equal height) so it sits flush in the column, and consider a subtle 'auto' label to explain why it differs.

verdict: Clean, calm first paint with a cyan accent that reads well. But the desktop two-column workspace is badly unbalanced: the form fills the left ~380px column while the right result card collapses to a tiny ~110px box holding one cyan pill, leaving a large empty right half and dead space below the card. Mobile stacks cleanly and looks good.
round1_held: Yes. Preview-only notice ('dispatching requires a Morpheus runtime token') is present, REQUESTS shows 0 as a clean empty state, digest placeholder is em-dash via digestPlaceholder. No regressions.

findings.title: Empty result column leaves a large desktop dead-zone
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the right result card is a short box containing only the cyan 'Run the form to preview the request payload.' pill, while the left form column is ~3x taller. The whole right half below the pill is empty white space. Code: ConsoleToolPanel.scss:150-155 sets the workspace to a 2-col grid (.console-tool__workspace) and ConsoleToolPanel.scss:357-365 caps the empty state at min-height:72px, so the result card never fills its column.
findings.fix: In ConsoleToolPanel.scss, give .console-tool__result a min-height that roughly matches the form (e.g. min-height: 100% via align-items: stretch on .console-tool__workspace, or min-height: 260px) and vertically center .console-tool__empty within it, so the waiting state is a deliberately centered card rather than a pill floating at the top of an empty column.

findings.title: Empty-state is a bare pill with no icon or guidance
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile: the result panel's only content before running is a single rounded pill 'Run the form to preview the request payload.' There is no icon, illustration, or hint about what the preview will contain (digest, payload rows). It reads as a placeholder, not a designed empty state.
findings.fix: In ConsoleToolPanel.tsx (the result block at lines 369-373), add a muted icon above the pill (e.g. a FileSearch/Braces lucide glyph) and a one-line subtext describing what appears after running ('Workflow, privacy mode and request digest will appear here'). Style in ConsoleToolPanel.scss .console-tool__empty.

verdict: Visually the strongest of the ConsoleToolPanel set: the form has four fields (Method/URL/JSON Path/Body) so the left column has more height, making the layout feel less empty than its siblings. Green accent is consistent. Still, the right result card collapses to a small pill leaving the right half empty on desktop. Mobile is clean.
round1_held: Yes. Preview-only notice present, REQUESTS 0 clean empty state, sensible default URL/JSON path prefilled so first paint is self-explanatory. No regressions.

findings.title: Right result column still half-empty on desktop
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the green 'Run the form to preview the request payload.' pill sits in a short card at the top-right; everything below it and to its right is empty white space down to the form's bottom edge. Same shared cause as the other consoles: ConsoleToolPanel.scss:150-155 + 357-365.
findings.fix: Same shared fix as compute-lab: stretch/center the empty result state in ConsoleToolPanel.scss so the waiting card fills and centers within its grid column instead of collapsing to 72px at the top.

findings.title: Body textarea placeholder is the only low-contrast element worth noting
findings.evidence: Desktop: the 'Optional POST body' placeholder in the Body textarea is noticeably lighter than the filled URL/JSON Path values. It's legible but is the faintest text on the screen.
findings.fix: This is acceptable for a placeholder; only worth darkening the placeholder token slightly (NeoInput placeholder color) if the design wants stronger contrast. No app-level change required.

verdict: The violet 'social' theme gives this console a distinct, pleasant identity vs the green/cyan siblings, and the violet empty pill is subtle and calm. Hero, notice and form read clearly. Desktop still suffers the shared unbalanced two-column dead-zone; mobile stacks well (heading wraps to two lines but is fine).
round1_held: Yes. Preview-only notice present, REQUESTS 0 clean, optional callback field clearly marked optional, sensible 'did:neo:testnet:sample-user' default. No regressions.

findings.title: Result column dead-zone on desktop (shared)
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: violet 'Run the form to preview the request payload.' pill in a short top-right card, with a large empty area below/right down to the form's bottom. Shared cause: ConsoleToolPanel.scss:150-155 + 357-365.
findings.fix: Apply the shared ConsoleToolPanel empty-state stretch/center fix so the waiting card fills its column.

findings.title: Distinct violet theme is the only one diverging from the oracle family hue
findings.evidence: appConfig.ts:32 sets theme family:'social', accentColor:'#a78bfa' (violet) while compute-lab is cyan, http/vrf are green, price is green. Side by side the six oracle consoles do not read as one family. This is intentional per-app theming and the violet looks good on its own, but flag for a consistency call.
findings.fix: If the team wants the six oracle consoles to feel like a suite, align accents to a shared oracle palette (or a small ordered set) in each appConfig.ts theme.accentColor. No change needed if per-app identity is the intent.

verdict: The best-looking console of the six. Full-width, balanced layout with a real live-price hero ($2.1940 NEO/USD), a green 'Fresh — updated 7m ago' freshness chip, and a clean Query feed card. No dead-zone because it does not use the shared two-column ConsoleToolPanel. Mobile reflows nicely with the three context tiles stacked.
round1_held: Yes. Staleness guard is visible and working (freshness chip 'Fresh — updated 7m ago'), em-dash placeholders for empty feed/network/source, friendly hint 'reads MorpheusDataFeed directly and never exposes a private RPC URL'. No regressions.

findings.title: Hero context tiles are right-heavy and slightly redundant with the price card
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the hero's right side stacks three full-width tiles (Feed 0x03013f49…, Network mainnet, Source on-chain mainnet RPC) while the left side has only the title + one line of copy, leaving the left lower area empty. 'Network mainnet' also partly duplicates info a user infers from the mainnet feed address. Code: PlayArea.tsx:65-78 price-hero__metrics.
findings.fix: In PlayArea.scss tighten the hero grid so the metrics column doesn't dominate (narrower max-width on price-hero__metrics, or render them as a compact inline meta row like the ConsoleToolPanel hero-meta), balancing the left/right weight.

findings.title: Feed address truncates to '0x03013f49…' with no copy affordance
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile: the Feed tile shows a truncated contract hash '0x03013f49…' with no way to copy or reveal the full value. For a 'keep the request path inspectable' tool, the inspectable identifier is partly hidden.
findings.fix: Add a copy-to-clipboard button or a title/tooltip with the full feed hash on the Feed metric (PlayArea.tsx:66-69), reusing the shared clipboard service so users can grab the address the console claims is inspectable.

verdict: Functionally identical layout to the other ConsoleToolPanel consoles, but the amber accent makes the whole first paint read like a warning rather than a calm tool: the hero shield badge, the info-notice icon, and the empty 'Run the form to preview' pill are all yellow/amber. Combined with the same right-side dead-zone, the empty state feels alarming where siblings feel neutral. Mobile same issue.
round1_held: Yes. Preview-only notice present, ENVELOPES 0 clean empty state, the description correctly clarifies 'non-cryptographic reference checksum (not encryption)'. No regressions.

findings.title: Amber accent makes the neutral empty state read as a warning
findings.evidence: Desktop + mobile screenshots: the hero badge, the 'Preview only' notice icon, and the empty-state pill 'Run the form to preview the request payload.' are all amber/yellow (#facc15 from appConfig.ts:29). Amber is the platform's warning color, so a brand-new, error-free console looks like it is flagging a problem — and it is the only one of the six that does this (siblings use calm green/cyan/violet).
findings.fix: Change theme.accentColor in oracle-seal-console/src/appConfig.ts:29 from '#facc15' to a non-warning hue (e.g. a teal/indigo such as the cyan #22d3ee used by compute-lab, or a sealed-input indigo), so the accent reads as 'private/sealed' rather than 'warning'. Reserve amber for actual warning states.

findings.title: Right result column dead-zone on desktop (shared)
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: amber pill in a short top-right card with the right half empty below it, same as the other ConsoleToolPanel consoles. Shared cause: ConsoleToolPanel.scss:150-155 + 357-365.
findings.fix: Apply the shared ConsoleToolPanel empty-state stretch/center fix.

verdict: Clean green-accented console. Sensibly hides the meaningless 'Requests' counter (hideRequestCount), so the hero meta line shows just Network + Endpoint, which looks tidier than the siblings' '0 requests'. Four prefilled fields give the form decent height. Still has the shared right-side result dead-zone on desktop; mobile is clean.
round1_held: Yes. Preview-only notice present, request counter correctly suppressed (hideRequestCount:true) so no '0' noise, defaults prefilled (consumer/salt/rounds/proof). No regressions.

findings.title: Result column half-empty on desktop (shared)
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the green 'Run the form to preview the request payload.' pill sits in a short top-right card; the area below it and to the right is empty down to the form's bottom edge. Shared cause: ConsoleToolPanel.scss:150-155 + 357-365.
findings.fix: Apply the shared ConsoleToolPanel empty-state stretch/center fix so the waiting state fills/centers its column.

findings.title: 'Rounds' numeric field gives no min/max or unit cue
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot: the Rounds field shows '1' with no helper text or visible bounds, so a user cannot tell the valid range for repeat count. The hero subtitle mentions 'repeat count' but the field itself has no constraint hint.
findings.fix: Add a placeholder or small helper note (e.g. '1-10') to the rounds field config in oracle-vrf-console/src/appConfig.ts, and/or clamp/validate the value in buildResult so an out-of-range repeat count surfaces a friendly warning row.
